top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at UCI Cyprus Gran Fondo. Practice on mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 63 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic UCI Cyprus Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
104ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
6,562ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At UCI Cyprus Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at UCI Cyprus Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of UCI Cyprus Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
6,562ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mountain passes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
63 miles on mountain passes burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Smooth pedaling at 63 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.
Low-cadence force work supports 6,562ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
